solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Economical type — watch — in pursuit of pub profit (7-6)

indicators.note: what follows is chasing, so it comes after the pub and profit

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
gain = profit
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover over the face

annotation.surface: A thrifty drinker keeps an eye on the pub's takings.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'watch' look like a verb aside; it is a noun, the old hunter pocket watch.
annotation.definitionFit: A bargain-hunter is someone out to spend as little as possible, an economical type.

entries.clue: Dog drinks and pants (5,6)

blocks.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
shorts are spirits served in small measures

annotation.surface: A dog laps up drinks and pants afterwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as a verb, panting dog; in British English pants are underpants.
annotation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose underpants, and pants in Britain means underwear.

entries.clue: Reignited, temperature turned to carbon old item (5)

indicators.note: one letter is changed into another

blocks.note: relit = reignited
T for temperature, the letter to be swapped out
C is the chemical symbol for carbon, which replaces the T

annotation.surface: A fire relit, its heat reduced to carbon ash.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is chemistry, a fire burning down to carbon; the instruction is purely a letter swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an old item.

entries.clue: Irish, excluding middle third, supporting current measure relating to frogs? (9)

indicators.note: drop the central three of the nine letters
in a down clue, the word below holds up the one above

blocks.note: the amp measures electric current
HIBERNIAN (Irish) loses its middle three letters, ERN

annotation.surface: Some Irish measurement of the electric current in frogs.
annotation.walkthrough: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish. The question mark flags that frogs are only one example of amphibians.
annotation.definitionFit: Amphibian as an adjective means relating to the class of animals that includes frogs.

entries.clue: Rise of an aroma just beginning (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising turns the word upwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned upwards
scent = aroma

annotation.surface: A smell starting to rise from the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a scent drifting up, which hides that only 'an' is turned.
annotation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, just beginning.

entries.clue: Skill rising when probing revolting part of plumbing (1-4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upwards
pushing inside the next word

blocks.note: art = skill, then turned upwards to TRA
people in revolt are up in arms, 'the people are up'

annotation.surface: A plumber's skill comes in handy when probing a disgusting drain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, fitting the drain; here it means rebelling, which is UP.
annotation.definitionFit: A U-trap is the U-shaped bend of pipe under a sink that holds water to block smells.

entries.clue: Possibly chance it over line of mechanical products? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are one possible arrangement of another
in a down clue, the anagram sits above the L

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
L for line

annotation.surface: Gambling on a product line of machinery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chance it' looks like a gamble on the line; the words are only the anagram letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical means relating to technology and machines, so of mechanical products.

entries.clue: Animal that jumps requiring a lot of space (3)

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: ROOM (space) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A kangaroo needs plenty of room to bound about.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true of a kangaroo, which hides that 'a lot of' is chopping ROOM.
annotation.definitionFit: Roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that moves by jumping.

entries.clue: Cut out large manœuvre by figure skater (4)

blocks.note: to axe something is to cut it out
L for large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A figure skater drops a big move from the routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut out large' sounds like dropping a big manoeuvre; it is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: An axel is a jump in figure skating with a forward take-off.

entries.clue: Historic swindle involving Young Conservative baker (10)

indicators.note: the swindle wraps round the young Conservative

blocks.note: past = historic
to rook someone is to swindle them; it opens after its first letter
Y for young
C for Conservative

annotation.surface: An old fraud involving a young Tory baker.
annotation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are Britain's main right-wing party, and Young Conservatives its youth wing.
annotation.definitionFit: A pastry cook makes pastries and cakes, a baker.

entries.clue: Consequences surrounding item of legislation for way of working (8)

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

blocks.note: the price of an action is its consequences
an act of Parliament

annotation.surface: The fallout around a new law and how it changes working methods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Consequences' as price is the stretch here: you pay the price for what you do.
annotation.definitionFit: A practice is a customary way of doing things, a way of working.

entries.clue: Cloak that’s for chop? (6)

blocks.note: the plain definition, a garment
the word the answer's own letters build when read as wordplay

annotation.surface: A cape worn for a butcher's work.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer after its first letter and after 'on', and it reads as an instruction to put P after the last three letters, which spells 'chop'. The question mark flags the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a hole for the head.

entries.clue: Final section of NY prison sentence after being out of prison? (4,7)

indicators.note: the sentence comes after the first piece

blocks.note: someone out of prison is home
a stretch is a term in prison

annotation.surface: An ex-con in New York serving the last part of a sentence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'NY' flags an Americanism: the British say home straight. The question mark admits that being home is only one way of being out.
annotation.definitionFit: The home stretch is the last part of a race or task, its final section.

entries.clue: Who’s quiet, working to pilfer? (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order

blocks.note: sh! is a call for quiet
anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Who is it that works quietly to steal things?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a shoplifter does work quietly to pilfer.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoplifter is someone who quietly steals goods from shops.

entries.clue: Observing the future, support first Conservative leaving in a rush (9)

indicators.note: the first C drops out of the word

blocks.note: prop = support
HECTIC (in a rush) without its first C

annotation.surface: A political forecast about a Tory quitting in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First Conservative' is the first C of HECTIC, not a party leader.
annotation.definitionFit: Prophetic means foretelling what is to come, observing the future.

entries.clue: Criticise demure article being presented in bright colour? (9)

indicators.note: the words are placed inside the colour

blocks.note: prim = demure
an is the indefinite article
red is a bright colour

annotation.surface: A sniffy critique of a modest feature printed in loud colours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of writing; it is the grammar word AN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reprimand is an official telling-off, so the verb means to criticise sharply.

entries.clue: Methodically search quantity of data stored on firm (4)

indicators.note: the data sits after the firm, as if saved onto it

blocks.note: Co. = company
MB = megabyte

annotation.surface: Trawling through a company's stored data.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the second piece after the first.
annotation.definitionFit: The image is a comb's teeth passing through hair and missing nothing, hence searching methodically.

entries.clue: Chamber group tour finishing early? Over (4)

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short of its end

blocks.note: TRIP (tour) without its last letter
O for over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: A string group's tour ends early and they call it over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like the end of the story; it is just the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians, a chamber ensemble.

entries.clue: Secure northern European cosmetic treatment (4,6)

blocks.note: to nail something down is to secure it
Poland is in northern Europe

annotation.surface: Locking down a beauty treatment from Scandinavia.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P of Polish is lost in the answer, a standard crossword disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: Nail polish is a lacquer applied to fingernails as a cosmetic.

entries.clue: Evidence of poor penmanship: I especially note a good deal around end of book (7)

indicators.note: the note wraps round the letter
the end of a word is its final letter, so the end of book is its K

blocks.note: as written
NB, nota bene, note well
the last letter of book, which goes inside NB
a lot = a good deal

annotation.surface: A teacher scrawls a note on a messy exercise book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Especially note' is a translation of nota bene, which is NB.
annotation.definitionFit: An inkblot is a smudge of spilt ink, the sign of messy handwriting.

entries.clue: That woman’s following key Dutch artist (6)

indicators.note: the woman's word comes after the key

blocks.note: the Escape key on a keyboard
her = that woman's

annotation.surface: She is the leading follower of a Dutch painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' tempts toward music (A to G); here it is a computer key.
annotation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist famous for impossible architecture.

entries.clue: Give new life to King meeting bridge opponents and bridge partners (5)

indicators.note: the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: R for rex, king
East and North sit next to each other and play against each other
East and West play as partners

annotation.surface: A king joins a bridge table to liven the game up.
annotation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West; N-S partner each other, as do E-W, so any mixed pair are opponents.
annotation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it, giving it new life.

entries.clue: Craftspeople showing outraged reaction about accepting shortened time (8)

indicators.note: 'about' as in about-turn: the word faces the other way
to accept something is to take it in, so the turned word holds the time inside it
the time loses its last letter

blocks.note: to kick up a stink is to protest loudly; then turned round to KNITS
TERM (a time, as in school term) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Artisans furious that their allotted time was cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' does the reversing here, not containing; 'accepting' does that job.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: knitting is one handicraft among many, so knitters are one kind of craftspeople.

entries.clue: Somewhat upset about iodine in bone (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down
the reversed word goes round the iodine
'iodine in bone' puts the iodine literally inside the letters that make the bone

blocks.note: a bit = somewhat, then upset to TIBA
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

annotation.surface: Mildly upset about the iodine dabbed on a bone injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat upset' reads as mildly distressed; 'somewhat' gives A BIT and 'upset' turns it over.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the shinbone is one bone of the leg among many in the body.

entries.clue: Each swirl of nostalgia overlooking old Saxon kingdom (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters are stirred round
to overlook something is to miss it out, so the O for old is skipped

blocks.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each
nostalgia without the O
O for old, the letter left out

annotation.surface: A wave of nostalgia for an ancient Saxon realm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition: it is the O dropped from nostalgia. East Anglia is the region of eastern England around Norfolk and Suffolk.
annotation.definitionFit: East Anglia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the East Angles, the modern region taking its name.

entries.clue: Support anyone in difficulties at the outset (3)

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Anyone In Difficulties

annotation.surface: Help whoever is struggling from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plea to help people in trouble, which is itself what the answer means.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving aid and giving support are the same act of help.

entries.clue: Number eight in cricket team in Somerset venue? (4)

blocks.note: the side that is 'in' is the one batting
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

annotation.surface: The number eight batsman at a Somerset ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number eight' reads as a batting position, which fits the cricket; it is the alphabet's eighth letter. Somerset is a county in south-west England with a cricket club.
annotation.definitionFit: Bath is a city in Somerset where the county has played cricket, hence a venue with a question mark.

entries.clue: Daughter, having reserve and humour, had worked with the risk intensely (4,4,5)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: D for daughter
icy reserve, a cool manner
wit = humour
anagram fodder, joined to the next word
anagram fodder; with HAD, six letters worked into a new order

annotation.surface: A cool, witty daughter who had played with danger.
annotation.walkthrough: Ice as reserve is a cold, distant manner. 'The risk' in the surface is split: 'the' is fodder, 'risk' starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: gambling with dice against death itself pictures taking the gravest risk.
